name: 34883-longctxdecode-dsv2lite-4gpu
hardware: 4x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (SM90), four GPUs of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:4), NVLink within the node.
parallelism: TP=4, DCP=4, PP=1, DP=1, expert parallelism off. One in-process vLLM engine; the other three ranks are worker processes it owns. The engine requires tensor-parallel-size % decode-context-parallel-size == 0.
architecture: DeepseekV2ForCausalLM MoE, 27 layers (layer 0 dense, 26 MoE), 64 routed + 2 shared experts, top-6, hidden 2048, bf16, ~30 GB of weights; attention is multi-head latent attention (16 heads, kv_lora_rank 512, head_size 576, v_head_dim 128); YaRN rope, max_position_embeddings 163840.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=4, bounded at 400 requests / 3600 s safety, first 25% by request count discarded as warmup.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, prompt exactly 32768 tokens and output exactly 1024 (min = max, so the backend forces ignore_eos), greedy. The chat template adds a few tokens, so the engine's own prompt count reads slightly above 32768; max-model-len 40960 leaves room for it.
purpose: A long-document analyst streaming 1024-token answers from 32k-token prompts, four concurrent users, mixture-of-experts model on four GPUs.
launch:
# The served engine, as `vllm serve --config` takes it. The request shape and the load profile
# are in scenario.json.
model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat

# Required, not decorative: this repo ships its config and modelling code behind `auto_map`, and
# the pinned transformers cannot resolve `deepseek_v2` without it.
trust-remote-code: true

tensor-parallel-size: 4
decode-context-parallel-size: 4
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 40960
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9
max-num-seqs: 32

# Equal to the declared prompt length, so each prompt is admitted in exactly one scheduler chunk.
max-num-batched-tokens: 32768
